question: does a pure-noise surface tag (unique per instance, no family information) capture the discovered latent as it grows to dominate the input string?
probe: each instance's 3 relabels share one tag -> tag capture inflates same-instance kNN recall; pure invariance keeps it at chance (~0.017). AE hyperparams frozen across tag_len; seed 0.
verdict: INVARIANT-ROBUST (mild salience gradient). At tag_len=64 the noise tag is >2x the formula content, yet family recall drops only 5.4pp (0.772->0.718) and instance (tag) recall rises to just 0.046 vs chance 0.017. Salience capture exists but is second-order; the algebraic family remains the dominant organizing axis of the latent.
ties_to_program: supports L1 (structure = algebraic, not lexical): surface-dominant nuisance strings do not hijack the representation. Consistent with P13 (discovery needs the right OPERATOR, not more capacity) -- the failure mode there is absence of the extracting transform, not salience hijack.
